title: Reasonable inferences and credibility
summary: An inference is a conclusion drawn from evidence about an unobserved or disputed fact. At summary judgment, reasonable favorable inferences belong to the nonmovant, while credibility and weight generally remain for trial.
notes: Favorable treatment does not require accepting an account no reasonable factfinder could believe. That limit should not become an excuse to choose the movant’s witnesses in an ordinary genuine dispute.

sections.How to work through the question: Identify the evidence, the proposed inference, the substantive issue it supports, and why a reasonable factfinder could draw it. Compare Matsushita’s contextual limits, Dyer’s unsupported hope of disbelief, Scott’s disputed video analysis, and Tolan’s correction of improper fact-weighing.
